extracted.intended_audience: members and officers of the District of Columbia Bar, Board of Governors, Bar administrators, and the District of Columbia Court of Appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Rules governing the organization, membership, governance, financial reporting, referendum and amendment procedures, and other administrative requirements for the District of Columbia Bar as promulgated to and governed by the D.C. Court of Appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble / Creation of official association
rubrics_metrics.description: The District of Columbia Court of Appeals ... does hereby create, as an official arm of the Court, an association of members of the Bar of the District of Columbia to be known as the District of Columbia Bar, and pursuant to its statutory authority governing admissions to the Bar promulgates the following rules for the government of the Bar and the individual members thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that the D.C. Bar is an official arm of the Court and that these Rules are promulgated under the Court's inherent and statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of Association — membership by admission
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons admitted to practice law in the District of Columbia are hereby organized as an association to be known as the 'District of Columbia Bar' subject to the provisions of the Rules hereinafter set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which individuals are members of the Bar (all persons admitted to practice in D.C.) and establishes the meaning of 'D.C. Bar' and other defined terms used in the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of the Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The purposes of the Bar shall be (a) to assist the legal profession in maintaining high standards of the practice of law in the District of Columbia; (b) to aid the courts ...; (c) to promote access to justice and enhance the delivery of legal services to those in need; (d) to foster and maintain ... high ethical standards; (e) to safeguard the proper professional interests of the members of the Bar; (f) to encourage the formation and support the activities of volunteer bar associations; (g) to provide a forum for and publish information about the practice of law, the science of jurisprudence and law reform, and the relationship of the Bar to the public; and (h) to carry on a continuing program of legal research and education ... and make reports and recommendations thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the official objectives and mission of the Bar which guide policy and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership — Persons Included
rubrics_metrics.description: All members of the Bar of the District of Columbia Court of Appeals shall be members of the District of Columbia Bar subject to due compliance with the conditions and requirements of such membership. Residence in the District of Columbia shall not be a condition of eligibility to membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that membership is coextensive with admission to practice and clarifies that residency in D.C. is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Course for New Admittees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bar shall establish and administer a course on the District of Columbia Rules of Professional Conduct and on District of Columbia practice. Within twelve months after admission to the Bar, all members shall, in accordance with procedures established by the Bar, complete such course and certify compliance with this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to complete the course or satisfy related requirements may result in suspension and inability to practice in D.C.; the Bar must report annually to the Court on the course addressing curriculum, faculty, number of presentations, attendance, and number of attorneys suspended for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of Membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The members of the District of Columbia Bar shall be divided into at least 4 classes known respectively as 'active' members, 'judicial' members, 'inactive' members, and 'retired' members. Definitions and eligibility criteria for each class are provided (e.g., inactive members are eligible for active membership but not engaged in practice and have requested enrollment as inactive; judicial members include judges and others who perform judicial functions; retired members must meet active-membership and years-of-practice thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how members may change class (written request and payment of dues as required), conditions under which judicial/inactive/retired members may not practice or vote, qualifications for retired status (active membership for five years, 25 years total practice, with limited substitutions), and grants the Board authority to create additional classes after consultation with the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: License Fees — ceiling, setting, and comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The District of Columbia Court of Appeals shall set a ceiling for annual license fees payable by any member. The Board of Governors shall determine the amount of license fees to be paid annually by members in the various classes of membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All license fees are paid to the Bar and fund its expenses; the Board may recommend changes to the Court (recommendations published and members given 60 days to comment or other period the Court directs). Recommendations by the Board for an increase in the dues ceiling shall not be subject to referendum under Rule VII. Non-payment of license fees may result in suspension and inability to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation and Reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: A member’s resignation from and reinstatement into the Bar shall be governed by procedures prescribed by the Bar, which shall include consultation with the Office of Disciplinary Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for resignation/reinstatement is delegated to the Bar but must involve consultation with disciplinary authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to the Clerk
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Bar shall forward forthwith, to the Clerk of this Court, the names of those attorneys who have registered with the Bar and those whose membership status has been changed in any way pursuant to the provisions of this Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes an administrative duty on the Bar's Secretary to keep the Court's Clerk updated on membership and status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers — composition and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers of the Bar shall be a President, a President-Elect, a Secretary, and a Treasurer, who shall be nominated and either elected or appointed in the manner provided in the Bylaws. Only active members ... shall be eligible to serve as officers of the Bar. The term of office of each officer shall be one year. The officers shall receive no compensation for their services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duties of officers and process for filling vacancies are set forth in the Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Governors — composition and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The affairs of the Bar shall be managed and directed by a Board of Governors consisting of the officers of the Bar and the Immediate Past-President of the Bar, and fifteen members elected by the members of the Bar in the manner prescribed by the Bylaws. The Treasurer-Elect shall be among the fifteen elected, non-officer members ... and shall serve as an at-large member of the Board after completing their year of service as Treasurer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may also appoint non-voting members per the Bylaws and has general charge of the affairs and activities of the Bar in accordance with these Rules and the Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: No opinion of the Bar on any matter involving legislation of major public interest or concern or of major importance to the members of the Bar shall be publicly expressed unless authorized by the Board of Governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires Board authorization before the Bar publicly expresses policy positions on matters of major public importance or member interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings of the Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an annual meeting of members of the Bar in a manner prescribed by the Bylaws. Special meetings of members of the Bar shall be called in a manner set forth in the Bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegates specifics of meeting procedures and calls to the Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum Procedure — Board initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors may at any time, by the affirmative vote of 2/3 of the Board, refer to the active members of the Bar for determination by member ballot, any question of Bar policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes the Board to place policy questions before the active membership via member ballot when 2/3 of the Board so votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum Procedure — members may initiate by petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors shall submit for determination by member ballot any question of Bar policy, including proposals for changes in the Rules or Bylaws, whenever directed so to do by a petition signed by not less than 3% of the active members of the Bar, based on the census of the Bar as of the first business day of the calendar year in which the petition is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the threshold for member-initiated referenda at 3% of active members (with census date specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum Procedure — ballot administration and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Ballots for use in any such referendum shall be prepared, distributed, returned and counted in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Board of Governors. The result of a referendum, as determined by a majority of the votes cast, when duly ascertained shall be published by the Board of Governors in the official Bar publication, and shall control the action of the Bar, the Board of Governors, the officers and committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that referendum procedures are governed by Board regulations; majority of votes cast controls and result must be published in official Bar publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursements — appropriations, accounting, audit, reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors shall make necessary appropriations for disbursements from the funds in the treasury to pay all necessary expenses of the Bar, its officers, employees, and committees. It shall be the duty of the Board of Governors to cause proper books of account to be kept and to procure an annual audit thereof by a certified public accountant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At each annual meeting the Board must present a financial statement showing assets, liabilities, receipts, and disbursements; a copy must be transmitted to the Clerk of the D.C. Court of Appeals and published in an official Bar publication prior to the annual meeting. The copy transmitted to the Clerk must be accompanied by a detailed statement reflecting all significant components of the Bar's total disbursements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylaws — adoption procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylaws not inconsistent with these Rules may be established by a majority vote of the voting members of the Board of Governors at a meeting with at least two-thirds of the voting Board members in attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies quorum/attendance requirement (at least two-thirds of voting Board members in attendance) and that adoption requires a majority of voting members present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Rules — presentation to the Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for amendment of these Rules may be presented to the Court by (a) petition of the Board of Governors; or (b) petition of the assembly in respect of changes approved by referendum as provided in Rule VII.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing upon such a petition will be pursuant to notice in such manner as the Court may direct; thus amendments proceed to the Court via Board petition or member-approved referendum petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Date of Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The District of Columbia Bar Rules shall take effect on April 1, 1972, on which date the association shall be deemed to have come into existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the effective date when the Bar is legally deemed to have come into existence under these Rules.
